source_snapshot.procedure:
【Before Test】
    1. Check that the SUT configuration (e.g., hardware, firmware, drivers, etc.) matches the specifications/recipe definition.
    2. Clear logs (e.g., dmesg, syslog, SEL, etc.).

    【During Test】
    Check CMOS Clear function
By Switch/Jumper
1. Power off system
2. Adjust clear CMOS switch/jumper
3. Restore the switch/jumper to default location
4. Power on system
5. Check onscreen POST message and see if POST prompt for input POP
6. Press F1 to enter uEFI and see if system prompt for input PAP
By Remove Battery
1. Change at least 5 types of setting, set PAP/POP and save settings
2. Exit setup and power off system after UEFI logo popup
3. Remove AC power source and all USB devices from MB.
4. Remove CMOS battery on the planar.
5. Waiting 10 mins before putting it back (If system spec define specific system discharge time, you can follow it.)
6. Power on system with CMOS battery intact
7. Check onscreen POST message and see if POST prompt for input POP
8. Press F1 to enter uEFI and see if system prompt for input PAP

    【After Test】
    1. Collect test results and photos, and save them to specific folders.
    2. Check if there are unexpected logs (e.g., dmesg, syslog, SEL, etc.) generate after test.
source_snapshot.criteria: 1. Check for Date & Time return to default (minimum) by Remove Battery. (Switch/Jumper will keep that you set.)2. Check the settings you set before test are returned to default. (Remove Battery/Switch/Jumper)3. The PAP/POP should NOT be cleared.4. Check POST event log.

historical_reviews.deepseek: NO. Correctly identifies the physical boundary but reduces the case to jumper state and omits the separate battery, BIOS settings, credentials and POST paths.
historical_reviews.gpt_v2: MANUAL ONLY / IMPROVED. V2 preserves both paths and their different reset expectations with board safety and recovery.

historical_reviews.v3_1: No V3.1 200-case record exists for this source key.

original_test_intent: Validate CMOS clearing through both the physical switch/jumper and battery-removal paths, including path-specific date/time and setting behavior, retained PAP/POP, POST/UEFI prompts and POST event evidence.
original_method: A qualified operator separately executes the de-energized jumper sequence and the AC/USB-disconnected battery sequence, establishes at least five BIOS settings and PAP/POP, records POST/UEFI outcomes, waits ten minutes or the specified discharge interval, and restores hardware/configuration.
manual_activity: Moving and restoring the CMOS jumper, removing/reinstalling the planar battery, disconnecting physical AC/USB, pressing F1 and inspecting POST/UEFI prompts are core human operations.
required_inputs: Exact board revision, jumper pin/default map and battery type/polarity
De-energization, AC/USB removal, discharge and ESD procedure
At least five selected BIOS settings with baseline/expected reset per path
Protected PAP/POP and boot/security recovery information
Console/OOB access, final state, qualified operator and one-user approval
safety_requirements: Never move the jumper or battery while energized; verify discharge and ESD controls.
Protect PAP/POP, boot keys and configuration backups before clearing CMOS.
Stop on ambiguous pin map, damaged holder, failed POST/boot or inability to restore hardware/default state.
Preserve each path's first outcome; no automatic repeat or silent reconfiguration.
agent_execution_scope: Collect read-only BIOS/BMC/SEL/host baselines and post-path event/boot evidence where interfaces permit.
Maintain the setting/credential/path evidence matrix and operator action timestamps.
Do not manipulate hardware, enter credentials or issue the formal verdict.
engineer_actions: Approve board procedure, settings and credential recovery.
Perform all physical actions and POST/UEFI observations for both paths.
Restore/verify the approved state and issue the verdict.

command_applicability.original_deepseek_command_fit: No software command can replace either physical path, but its description omits most acceptance coverage.
command_applicability.command_recommendation: Retain both source physical methods and use read-only firmware/event interfaces only for corroboration.
command_applicability.original_parameters_and_time_preserved: Both paths, five settings, PAP/POP, ten-minute/spec discharge option, POST event and 5/20-minute fields are preserved.

modernized_recommendation.status: RETAIN DUAL PHYSICAL PATH WITH PATH-SPECIFIC MATRIX
modernized_recommendation.recommended_method: Use board-revision-specific checklists and a before/after matrix for date/time, five settings, PAP/POP prompts, POST messages/events and restored hardware position.
modernized_recommendation.supported_version: Record board, BIOS, BMC and CPLD revisions.
modernized_recommendation.official_reference: Owner board service manual and BIOS CMOS-clear/PAP/POP specification.
modernized_recommendation.difference_from_original_method: Adds identity, credential safety and recovery evidence without replacing physical operations.
modernized_recommendation.coverage_difference: No loss; jumper and battery paths remain separate.
modernized_recommendation.required_inputs: Board map, discharge SOP, setting matrix and protected credentials.
modernized_recommendation.risks_limitations: Remote configuration reads cannot prove physical jumper/battery manipulation or screen prompts.

project_override_considerations: A platform-specific discharge time may replace ten minutes exactly as the source allows, but must be recorded. Projects may add setting checks, not collapse the two physical paths without an explicit coverage override.
expected_evidence: Board/jumper/battery/power/ESD specification, selected settings, credential backup and authorization
Timestamped physical actions and restored jumper/battery/AC/USB state for each path
Path-specific BIOS date/time/settings, PAP/POP and POST/UEFI/event records
Recovered boot/host/BMC health and separate engineer verdict

source_conflict_analysis.analysis: The criteria distinguish date/time retention on the jumper path from broader setting reset; the two path-specific expectations are unusual but not directly contradictory and require an owner matrix.

blocked_analysis.analysis: Board documentation and credentials are readiness inputs. With them, a qualified operator can execute both defined physical paths.

comparison_to_prior_reviews.deepseek: Agree with NO but restore battery path, settings, PAP/POP, POST and recovery coverage.
comparison_to_prior_reviews.gpt_v2: Agree with MANUAL ONLY and its dual-path safety model.
comparison_to_prior_reviews.v3_1_improvement: Keeps supporting agent evidence distinct from manual physical and screen acceptance.

review_improvement: Prevents a simple jumper-position note from being mistaken for full CMOS functional coverage across two destructive configuration paths.
independent_technical_reasoning: The case deliberately tests two motherboard-level mechanisms and direct POST/UEFI behavior. Neither physical action nor screen interaction can be established by remote telemetry alone, so the entire acceptance remains MANUAL ONLY.
